recipes.name: Chicken Provencal
ingredients_raw: 1.5 cups canned crushed tomatoes with their juice
0.33 cup black olives, such as Nicoise or Kalamata, halved and pitted

steps.text: Heat oil in a large, deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with 1/4 teaspoon each of the salt and pepper and put it in the pan. Cook the chicken until browned, turning, about 8 minutes in all. Remove the chicken from the pan. Pour off all but 1 tablespoon fat from the pan.

Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add onion and garlic and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion starts to soften, about 3 minutes. Add the wine to the pan and simmer until reduced to about 1/4 cup, 1 to 2 minutes. Add tomatoes, rosemary, thyme, olives, anchovy paste, and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and simmer for 5 minutes.

Add the chicken thighs and drumsticks and any accumulated juices. Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 10 minutes. Add the breasts and cook until the chicken is just done, about 10 minutes more. Stir in the remaining 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Provencal
raw_recipe.description: Chicken Provencal provides comforting French-inspired flavor thanks to the dish's staples like tomatoes, olives, herbs, and wine.

review.reviewBody: What an amazing dish! So much depth of flavor, and fairly simple too! You're going to need quite a large pan, so aim for at least 12-14" in diameter. I ended up using a more crushed tomatoes - the can size was 15 ounces (instead of the 12 ounces called for) and that turned out to be a good amount. I used Kalamata olives and they brought the perfect flavor to the dish. I suggest doubling the anchovy paste - even at 2 teaspoons, I couldn't taste it, other than the very subtle saltiness. I cooked all the pieces for 20 minutes, instead of adding the breasts in during the last 10. They would not have been cooked enough, so this was just easier. A very impressive dish that you could serve guests!
Will definitely make again, might add mushrooms 👍🏻
Excellent. Using a whole chicken is a bit much even for 4. Next time I will try it with chicken thighs
Easy fast to make with delicious results

Oh my gosh, this was so good. I used a 10" pan that was fairly deep and it worked out fine.I also used 2.96 lb of bone-in, skin on, Thighs. I probably added a little more black olives (a few green too). Instead of the last 1/2 teaspoon of salt, i added a full teaspoon of concentrated chicken stock. Oh, and on step one where it says to pour out all but one tablespoon of fat, i forgot to do that. No biggie, I ended up spooning the rich sauce of roasted cubed potatoes. I will be making this for others whenever I want to impress someone.
Have made this several times big hit with family. Have had with mashed potatoes, egg noodles and rice all good.

Not too bad! I wouldn't say I loved it but it had a pretty good taste to it. Enough that I will make it again. I don't have to throw away that anchovy paste now. 😊I just cut up thighs and it came out pretty good. 4.5 stars. Mine wasn't as red though. It's weird how it never comes out looking like the picture.

Comfort flood for a chilly fall evening. The only change I made was to add half a bulb of fennel with the onion, just because I had it leftover from another recipe. I felt it did add a bit more Provence to the dish.

I like crushed tomatoes but ended up using some homegrown roasted tomatoes I had already defrosted for a different dish before changing to this one. Subbed white wine for red, smashed an anchovy filet with salt to make a paste, used kalamata olives, and served it over linguine. Excellent flavor, but next time want to see how it tastes with a bit of French red pepper added.
Really flavorful! The olives do have a strong presence, so be sure your guests like olives.
